historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 guidance (net flows A$18-20bn on A$135.7bn opening FUA) less ~2%/yr revenue-margin compression; equity CAGR rejected, see warning
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (11.7%) is ~45% below revenue (20.9%) and adjusted EPS (20.0%) CAGRs. Cause: a capital-light business paying out ~80% of earnings, plus the FY2026 FG charge cutting equity from 199.1 to 161.9. Book value is not a growth proxy here.
historical_growth.notes: EPS and FCF CAGRs use FG-normalised FY2026 (adjusted EPS 55.2c; owner FCF 110.4 before lease principal, for comparability with earlier years). On statutory FY2026 they are meaningless: EPS 3yr -3.5%, owner FCF 3yr about -18%. Owner-FCF series (FCF - SBC - interest received): FY2021 ~35.5, FY2022 53.2, FY2023 68.1, FY2024 76.5, FY2025 110.5, FY2026 110.4 normalised (37.2 statutory). Normalised owner FCF was flat FY2025 to FY2026 despite revenue +21%: capex nearly doubled (7.9 to 13.5) and payments to suppliers and employees rose 28%. FY2021 revenue and EPS are blank in the Metrics CSV; the 5yr revenue CAGR uses FY2021 revenue of ~148 implied by underlying EBITDA 79.3 at a 53.5% margin, and the 5yr EPS CAGR uses underlying NPAT 54.1 over ~243.5M shares. FY2020 to FY2026 revenue CAGR from reported figures is 21.1%. SBC is ~0.5% of revenue throughout, so reported and owner FCF CAGRs barely differ.

scenario_narratives.base: Netwealth keeps taking share as one of two independent specialist platforms, but not at the pace its Dx30 ambition requires. FY2027 net flows fall inside the guided A$18-20bn on A$135.7bn of opening FUA; with modest market growth and platform revenue/average FUA drifting down from 30.7bps, revenue grows 15% in FY2027 and decelerates to 5% by year 10. The model-basis EBITDA margin drops from 49.1% to 44.5% in FY2027 (guided ~47% on the company basis, less Program RISE project costs and the Paradino loss, which are real cash), then recovers to ~50.5% as the largely fixed technology base scales. Capitalised software runs at the guided ~A$17M and capex stays near 4% of revenue. First Guardian is closed apart from the class-action provision in the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: Dx30 is delivered. FUA doubles by FY30 as legacy bank and insurer platforms keep leaking assets, Netwealth Private brings high-net-worth balances, and the Morgan Stanley relationship opens the individual-HIN broking market. Managed-account FUM keeps growing faster than FUA, offsetting administration-fee tiering, so revenue grows 18% in FY2027 and stays in double digits through year 7. Operating leverage takes the margin to 54%, above the FY2021 peak, and the class action is dismissed or settled inside the bridge provision.
scenario_narratives.bear: The First Guardian episode proves more costly than the cash already paid. Licensees and advisers favour HUB24 in new mandates, net flows undershoot guidance, and an equity-market drawdown reduces average balances; revenue growth falls to 10% and then to mid single digits. Fee caps and price competition compress the revenue margin faster than volume grows the cost base, cash-rate cuts thin the pooled-cash margin, and the APRA enforceable undertaking leaves a permanently heavier governance cost base, holding the margin at 42-44%. A class-action outcome above the bridge provision would come on top of this path and is not in the flows.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the platform on normalised, ex-First-Guardian owner cash flow built from components, starting at FY2027 guidance rather than at the FY2026 statutory trough or a peak margin. The FG cash cost is already in the balance sheet; the residual exposure is a visible bridge provision and a heavier bear weight, not a discount-rate premium. Growth is anchored below management's Dx30 ambition in the base case and at it in the bull case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Class action (lodged September 2026) is unquantified; the A$30M bridge provision is a placeholder judgment worth A$0.12/share
Revenue margin (platform revenue/average FUA) has fallen 33.6 to 30.7bps in three years; each further 1bp is ~3% of revenue at near-100% decremental margin
FUA is market-sensitive: a 10% equity drawdown removes roughly a year of net-flow growth from the revenue base
Program RISE project costs are excluded from guided margin and not quantified; the model assumes ~1.5% of revenue for two years
Terminal value is the majority of value and the Gordon terminal binds below the 20x cap; a 1pt WACC change moves the value materially (see sensitivity)
Cash-fee revenue (~15% of revenue) depends on the RBA cash rate and the margin on pooled client cash

inputs.share_count_basis: 245,396,703 fully paid ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY2026 AR note on issued capital) plus ~0.5M dilutive LTI options/rights (EPS note: 495,366) = ~245.9M fully diluted. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: NORMALISED, not statutory. Statutory FY2026 FCF was 46.15 (OCF 59.626 less capex 13.476) after the one-off First Guardian (FG) outflow. Normalised = 46.15 + 105.244 FG expenses (100.726 compensation + 4.518 legal/consulting) - 32.040 FG tax effect (company's own adjusted-NPAT reconciliation) - 1.993 lease principal (financing line, treatment B) = 117.37. The FG tax shield is taken at the P&L figure; part of the cash benefit may land in FY2027 tax instalments.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report: share-based payment expense 2,060 ($'000), income statement and cash-flow reconciliation. No net-share-settlement tax line exists (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in every period).
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built, all-equity (the A$58.3M term loan is transitional FG funding). Australian 10-year government bond ~4.4% + beta ~1.05-1.1 x ~5.5% ERP = ~10.3%; rounded to 10.0% for a recurring, basis-point-fee revenue base. One WACC for all three scenarios: regulatory, litigation and competitive risk is carried in the flows, the bridge and the weights, not stacked on the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. FY2026 lease cash = 1.993 principal + 0.524 interest = 2.52 (0.66% of revenue), charged via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (12.079) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (8.155 total less 2.172 ROU = 5.98, 1.56% of revenue).
inputs.interest_treatment: Net cash (91M) is below 1x the FCF base, so the strip is not mandatory, but it is applied anyway for a clean match: interest received (6.924) is removed from the EBITDA margin and from last_fcf, and the cash plus the A$24M term deposit that earn it are in net debt and the bridge.
inputs.ebitda_margin_definition: ebitda_margin_path is on PLATFORM REVENUE (382.901), before SBC, before lease cash, and excluding interest income. FY2026 on that basis: (192.934 adjusted EBITDA + 2.060 SBC - 6.924 interest) / 382.901 = 49.1%. The company's own margin is on total income (391.127) after SBC and including interest: 49.3%. FY2027 guidance of ~47% is on the company basis and excludes FG and Program RISE project costs; on the model basis that is ~46.8%, before the RISE costs (unquantified; ~1.5% of revenue assumed) and Paradino's ~A$3M EBITDA loss (~0.7%), which the model charges because they are real cash.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US adaptations (AUD WACC, lease treatment B, no NCI). Routed via dcf-methods: Netwealth is an operating company earning bps fees on client assets it administers but does not own; client FUA and pooled cash are off balance sheet, so it is not a deposit taker or balance-sheet financial and the FCF/net-debt framework means what the engine assumes. FY2026 NORMALISED: statutory FY2026 (EBITDA 87.7, NPAT 60.7, FCF 46.2) carries the one-off A$105.2M First Guardian charge and is not used as the base; the forward build starts from adjusted (ex-FG) economics and FY2027 guidance. The FG cash is already out of the balance sheet (the term loan funding it is in net debt), so it is charged once. Remaining FG exposure (class action lodged September 2026, unquantified) is a judgment provision in the equity bridge plus the bear weight. Adjusted EBITDA: the annual report's reconciliation shows 192.934; the 191.5 figure quoted elsewhere in this run was not found in the filing and is not used. Share count history before FY2022 is not in the Metrics CSV; only the latest count matters to the model. Non-repurchaser: buyback_cash is 0 and the flat count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge (SBC is 0.5% of revenue, so the convention is nearly costless here). Paradino acquisition (announced September 2026, up to ~A$29-39M including earn-outs) is post balance date and treated as value-neutral cash-for-asset; its guided FY2027 EBITDA loss is inside the year-1 margin. No Q1 FY2027 quarterly update was in the extracted filings; year 1 rests on the August 2026 guidance.

bear.narrative: First Guardian damages the gatekeeper brand: adviser wins slow, HUB24 keeps taking share, and flows fall well short of guidance while a weak equity market trims balances. Fee tiering and competition cut the revenue margin faster, and permanent post-RISE compliance cost plus feature reinvestment hold margins in the low 40s.

base.narrative: Net flows land in the guided A$18-20bn range and FUA compounds in the mid-teens, short of the Dx30 ambition (doubling FUA by FY30 needs ~19%/yr). Revenue margin keeps slipping ~0.5-0.8bps a year. Margin dips in FY27-28 on Program RISE and Paradino, then operating leverage returns it to ~50%.

bull.narrative: Dx30 is met: FUA doubles by FY30 on share gains from legacy platforms, Netwealth Private and the Morgan Stanley HIN/broking relationship. Fee compression stays mild, the class action settles for little, and the fixed technology base delivers margins above the prior 53.5% peak.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a live, unquantified class action, an APRA enforceable undertaking with independent oversight, and a single-regulator, single-market dependency. Base 50%: guidance is specific and the FY2026 operating numbers (FUA +20%, net flows A$15.4bn) support it. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs Dx30 delivered, fee compression contained and a benign litigation outcome together, while HUB24 has recently been gaining share faster.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
